summary: The home of a hugely used open-source UI family, built like documentation rather than a showcase: a plain white page with a sticky text nav, a title-and-Download landing, copy-paste CSS usage, editable weight-by-weight sample lines, a yellow table of every OpenType feature off vs on, and a green glyph inspector with an optical-size slider over 2,800 glyphs. Language list, FAQ and trademark line sit past the 30,000px capture limit (HTML only).

instances.look: Sticky 48px white bar: 'Inter' (bold, 14px) at the left, Features · Glyphs · FAQ · Lab · Download ↓ at the right; it is stitched over the crops of every block below

White page: 'The Inter / typeface family' in two lines of tight bold display type (~180px), then an 8-column row: tagline 'The 21st century standard' with a small black 'Download ↓' pill, and two columns of small explanatory text with inline links ('2000 glyphs', '147 languages')
instances.ux: One primary button (Download ↓ → /inter/download/); inline links jump to #glyphs, #languages and #features
instances.learn: For a utility family the hero can be a doc page header: name huge, one-line claim, one button, and the spec (glyph count, languages, weights, opsz) as linked facts

reconstruction.layout: Full width, ~980px tall, page margin ~66px; h1 spans the row (2 lines); below, an r-grid of 8 columns: cell 1–2 tagline + button, cell 3–5 paragraph (~470px), cell 6–8 paragraph (~470px); text columns start ~110px under the title
reconstruction.typography: Title ~180px InterVariable Bold/SemiBold (display opsz 32), tracking ~-0.03em, leading ~0.95; tagline 14px Regular; body 14px Regular, leading ~1.45, links underlined; button 12px Medium white on black, radius 4px
reconstruction.content: Real product copy: workhorse UI typeface, 2000+ glyphs, 147 languages, weights 100–900, text and display optical sizes, true italic; 'one of the world's most used typefaces'
reconstruction.html: r-grid[columns=8] > r-cell[span=row] h1.title + r-cell[span=1-2] (tagline, a.button) + r-cell[span=3-5] + r-cell[span=6..]

instances.look: Every weight from Thin 100 to Black 900 as one editable line at ~144px ('Salient gazelle eyes', 'Internationalization', 'Botanica Francisco', 'Hamburgefonstiv'), each with a tiny grey style name left and weight number right; then the same for the italics ('Inorganic compound', '3 hours till midnight', 'United Martians'); then each weight again as a 2–3 line sentence at ~86px ('Chemistry is a physical science…', 'The Sicilian Defense is a chess opening that begins with 1.e4 c5')

instances.learn: Give every weight its own phrase rather than one repeated pangram: the list reads like a stream of small facts, and the labels (name + number) teach the weight scale

instances.look: A chrome-yellow section 'Features' with a white 'altG16I' set with alternates at top right, then a ruled three-column table Feature | Off | On: each row a monospace tag chip (calt, dlig, tnum, frac, case, ccmp, sups, subs, sinf, dnom, numr, zero, ss01–ss08) with name and note, and the same sample twice; in the Off column the glyphs that will change are tinted darker; ends (in block 09) with a 'Listing of all features' in four columns of tags
instances.ux: static: no toggles; Off and On are rendered side by side with font-feature-settings 0/1
instances.learn: Tint the characters a feature will affect in the 'off' sample: readers see where to look before comparing with 'on'

instances.look: Back on white, five topics each shown as two or three stacked display lines, default first then with alternates on: '1234567890' (alternative digits), 'Guillable ürá' ('Character variants is a mood'), 'Efficient after' (compact f and t), a tabular-figure block in mixed weights, 'Illusion A03 / Illusion A0̸3' (disambiguation), 'It's "fun" here, Möbius' ×3 (quote styles); each with a caption and a list of the tags used
instances.learn: Stack default and alternate versions of the same display line directly on top of each other, so the eye catches only the glyphs that change

instances.look: A green section headed 'Glyphs' in white: on the left a sticky inspector (toolbar with an 'Optical size' slider, 'Small opsz' and 'Details' switches, glyph name 'A' and 'U+0041', a small preview) above a canvas showing the selected glyph ~500px on white Cap height / x-height / Baseline lines; on the right a 10-column grid of 2,811 glyphs in hairline cells, grouped by base letter with every accented and Greek/Cyrillic look-alike next to it
instances.ux: Click a cell to load it into the inspector (URL hash #glyphs/<name>); drag opsz 14–32 or toggle Small opsz; 'Details' toggles construction details on the canvas; the inspector stays pinned while the ~19,000px grid scrolls; cells have a title tooltip with glyph name, code point and Unicode name
instances.learn: Order the grid by base letter, not by code point (A, Ä, Ã, …, Greek Α, Cyrillic А): it shows how far each letter's family extends, and the pinned inspector keeps the page usable at 2,800 glyphs
